title: Event Horizon: causal map + retry time-lens for compact failure triage
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design an integrated, compact debugging surface for the Redwood Console that helps engineers triage failed requests by showing causal relationships, retry timeline, payload diffs and rollout context without leaving a single pane. The "Event Horizon" concept combines a causal graph (compact nodes for requests, retries, downstream calls), a horizontal time-lens showing retry/backoff events and latency spikes, and a minimap scrubber to navigate dense sequences. Focus is on fast root-cause hypothesis generation: surface likely root causes, candidate fixes, and links to rollout metadata (commit, canary group, region).
problem_statement: Operators currently hop between traces, raw payloads, and rollout dashboards to understand a failure progression. This workflow is slow and error-prone when failures include many retries, fallback paths, or when rollouts/variant toggles may be correlated with errors. We need a single compact view that preserves rich context (payload KV diffs, error taxonomy, model variant) and supports playback and export for incident reports.
goals: Allow an engineer to go from 'I see an error spike' to 'I can hypothesize root cause + mitigation' in under 5 minutes
Visualize retry/backoff timing and how retries change payload/headers over time
Correlate request failures with rollout metadata (model variant, region, capacity tier) and flag likely rollout candidates
Provide a compact minimap and time-lens to navigate high-throughput traces
Preserve privacy: redact PII by default and surface a secure reveal flow for authorized users
out_of_scope: Full incident timeline export to external SIEMs (we will link to existing export flows)
Replacing full trace view in Console's Trace Explorer; Event Horizon is a triage surface, not a retrospective forensic tool
design_notes: Primary canvas: left column causal map (nodes are requests, retries, downstream calls); central lane: time-lens with sequenced ticks for request/response events; right column: compact payload inspector with KV fold, inline diff and k/v highlight for changed keys
Nodes encode error taxonomy via color + icon; hover surfaces show quick metadata (status code, latency, model id, commit hash)
Minimap with density heatmap for event volume; scrubbing updates main time-lens and causal map focus
Playback controls: step-forward by attempt, play with adjustable speed, and jump-to-likely-root-action (heuristic based on error frequency and change points)
Rollout strip anchored above time-lens: shows active deployment variants with hover to reveal percent traffic and link to rollout config
Accessibility: keyboard-first scrubbing, high-contrast palette, text-size scaling for dense timelines
Privacy & security: default PII redaction, explicit reveal button opens modal with audit log link and requires RBAC scope 'payload-view'
tradeoffs_and_concerns: Rendering: a causal map for extremely high fanout can be noisy — we will cap visible nodes and provide 'expand' affordances and progressive disclosure
Performance: client-side render of many events may tax browser on large traces; plan to sample and progressively fetch detail blocks
Accuracy of root-cause heuristics: keep heuristics conservative and surface confidence scores rather than deterministic claims
Security: exposing payload diffs increases risk; must require audit trail and opt-in reveal with KMS-backed logging
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma mock that demonstrates causal map + time-lens + payload inspector interactions
Clickable prototype: scrub minimap updates time-lens and loads payload diffs for selected tick
Payload inspector shows inline KV diff and a secure 'reveal' flow requiring RBAC scope
Rollout strip displays variant names, percentage of traffic, and links to rollout detail; clicking a variant filters causal map to requests that used that variant
Design handoff artifacts: annotated tokens, color variables, component specs and edge-case behaviors documented in the PRD
Sign-off from PM (product), Eng (runtime/instrumentation), and Security on the reveal flow
implementation_notes: Backend will need a single compact API that returns: event sequence, node graph edges, per-event metadata, and payload snapshots (redacted) with pointers to full payloads requiring additional auth
Prefer server-side diff generation for payloads to avoid heavy client CPU work; return summary keys to render fold/expand UI
Integrate with rollout metadata service to fetch active variant coverage and commit links
Expose as an optional Console route behind feature-flag 'event-horizon' for staged rollout
open_questions: Should the causal map show inferred causal edges (heuristic-based) or only explicit trace-referenced edges?
What level of payload redaction is allowed for on-call rotation vs. SRE with elevated privileges?
How does Event Horizon interact with existing trace retention and sampling policies when events are missing?
